scenario: On one operator-reported CoreBoard V1.2 sample, verify normal-image WPA2-PSK and strict-SAE completion, IPv4/DNS configuration, gateway reachability, scan continuity, and configured NOR multiuser network startup.
expected: Both handshakes complete; network configuration and basic reachability remain available in bounded checks, including after the normal NOR boot path.
observed: On the normal RAM image, strict SAE with local ieee80211w=2 reached WPA_COMPLETED and remained COMPLETED for about five minutes. DHCPv4 assigned an IPv4 /24 configuration and nameserver; DNS resolved example.com, and the gateway returned 3/3 replies for both small and 1400-byte ICMP probes. WPA2-PSK reached WPA_COMPLETED with CCMP pairwise/group ciphers; the supplicant observed EAPOL M1–M4 once each. A bounded scan preserved the link and exposed two same-SSID BSSIDs; before explicit ROAM, a new COMPLETED state was observed on the second BSSID. The RSN app-IE ownership fix uses vendor-owned copy mode, and the auth_done fix sends common controlled-port authorization through the bounded radio worker once per join generation. The SAE AP observer had no capture delta, so SAE completion and IGTK installation rely on supplicant/driver reports. An ordinary POWER reboot of the previously installed NOR FIT started wpa_supplicant and dhcpcd automatically without rcorder error; SAE profile 3 reached COMPLETED with CCMP and STATUS pmf=1, IPv4 and DNS example.com succeeded, and the hostname was ember-mosaico-01. A replacement 10 MiB LittleFS root (SHA-256 recorded in inputs) was then written at 0x600000 and passed esptool verification; it was tested with a RAM diagnostic kernel, but a normal NOR boot of this replacement root is not yet verified. With the mDNS service started and /bin/hostname confirmed as ember-mosaico-01, host A queries for ember-mosaico-01.local received no response over either legacy-unicast UDP/5353 or multicast UDP/5353 (TTL 255), each within a 3-second window. Cause is undetermined. A separate TCP roundtrip transferred 65,536 bytes in each direction with matching SHA-256. A later bounded scan exposed two same-SSID BSSIDs. A subsequent explicit fresh-cache ROAM request returned OK; teardown began with rescan requested and was followed by station disconnect reason 8. Transition completion and a new association were not confirmed. In a later, separate diagnostic scan (not a new ROAM), the native stop/start path reported teardown generation 2, error 0, and rescan requested; this confirms return from that control path, not scan completion. A management-helper timeout produced no marker, panic, or OOM evidence and does not establish a kernel hang. This is bounded connectivity evidence, not sustained reliability or roaming acceptance.

limits: One operator-reported V1.2 sample; this does not establish support for other revisions.
SAE remained COMPLETED for about five minutes during this bounded session; this does not establish long-duration reliability.
A 65,536-byte TCP transfer and return passed with matching host SHA-256; throughput and sustained reliability were not measured.
802.11k/v/r and BTM/RRM behavior are under investigation and were not validated here.
No forged-frame protection test has been completed.
STATUS pmf=1 means AP MFPC set/MFPR clear; local ieee80211w=2 is the independent required-PMF policy.
The SAE AP observer had no capture delta; SAE completion and IGTK installation rely on supplicant/driver reports, not independent AP-side capture.

The replacement LittleFS root was written and tested with a RAM diagnostic kernel; a normal NOR boot with that replacement root remains unverified. The daemon started, but host queries for the verified hostname received no mDNS response over unicast or multicast; cause is undetermined.

A later bounded scan exposed two same-SSID BSSIDs. A fresh-cache explicit ROAM returned OK; teardown began with rescan requested and disconnect reason 8 followed, but transition completion and a new association remain unconfirmed. A separate later diagnostic scan reported stop/start generation 2, error 0, rescan requested; it was not a new ROAM and scan completion was not established. A management-helper timeout alone does not establish a kernel hang.
